before: Rejecting a proposed paragraph mark, or accepting a deleted one, joined the paragraph into the one after it and kept the second paragraph's node. An undo of the split that proposed the mark removes the second paragraph instead. When one participant rejected a tracked split while its author undid it, each edit removed the paragraph the other kept, and every replica lost the whole paragraph.
after: The joined paragraph is the first one, with its attributes, the properties of the mark that remains, and the content of every joined paragraph in order, as a join by deleting a mark keeps the paragraph before it. A rejection and an undo of the same split both keep the first paragraph, so its text survives on every replica.
reason: Only the editor's resolution of the decision changes, and its journal writes ordinary moves, removals, and text copies that released replicas already read. No stored field, identity, conflict rule, or canonical mapping changes, so a mixed room converges. A released replica that makes the decision keeps the second paragraph until it upgrades, so the race can still lose the paragraph when that replica decides.
